slip_gp_fit — DRIVE roverslip op

• Data kinds: signal × signal → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.slip_gp_fit(slopes, slips, length_scales=None, noise_levels=None) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import roverslip; roverslip.slip_gp_fit(slopes, slips, length_scales=None, noise_levels=None) -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("slip_gp_fit"))

Usage

Gaussian process from slope angle to slip ratio (RBF kernel + homoscedastic observation noise). Hyperparameters by grid search on the log marginal likelihood.

y is fitted after subtracting the mean and dividing by the standard deviation (signal variance fixed at σ_f² = 1; searches over ℓ and noise σ_n). The default length_scales is 16 steps (log-spaced) from 0.05 to 2 times the angle range, and noise_levels is 16 steps from 0.01 to 1 (in units of normalised y). The return value is a dict used for prediction (kind = "gp", x, alpha, L, ell, noise, y_mean, y_scale, log_marginal_likelihood). For data whose noise varies with angle (heteroscedastic), the band has the width of the overall average (a trap for the gate).
